creator: Seamless Communication, Meta AI (Meta AI Research)
description: A subset of SeamlessAlign — the largest open multimodal speech translation corpus — covering the English (enA) to Hindi (hiA) language direction, with speaker embeddings computed using the XLS-R 2B model. SeamlessAlign was created by automatically mining and aligning speech and text data across 37 languages, totaling 470,000 hours, using SONAR multilingual embeddings and a margin-based mining criterion.
name: seamless-align-enA-hiA.speaker-embedding.xlsr-2b
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: SeamlessAlign uses automatic alignment rather than human annotation. Speech and text segments are projected into a shared SONAR multilingual embedding space, and pairs are identified using a margin-based similarity criterion (threshold 1.15). The mining process compares all speech segments in one language against all segments in another (global mining) using FAISS for efficient similarity search.
rai:dataBiases: Gender representation analysis shows masculine representation is predominant in the SeamlessAlign mined data. The dataset is derived from web-crawled audio, which may over-represent certain domains, speakers, and demographics. Hindi is classified as a medium-resource language, meaning coverage may be uneven compared to high-resource languages.
rai:dataCollection: SeamlessAlign was created through automatic parallel data mining. Starting with 4 million hours of raw audio from publicly available crawled web data, the pipeline applied speech language identification (LID), voice activity detection (VAD)-based over-segmentation, and SONAR-based multilingual embedding to mine aligned speech-text and speech-speech pairs. For Hindi specifically, 15,118 hours of raw audio were available, with 150 hours of ASR transcriptions used to train the speech encoder.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw audio from a publicly available repository of crawled web data (4 million hours total across all languages). For Hindi (hin), 15,118 hours of raw audio were available. On the text side, the same sentence-segmented dataset from NLLB was used.
rai:dataLimitations: The mining process uses a threshold-based approach (Sonar score ≥ 1.15) that may include noisy alignments. The over-segmentation strategy increases the number of segments 8x, introducing noise in the embedding space. Mining was focused on 37 languages; Hindi is a medium-resource language with only 15,118 hours of raw audio. The mined data tends to produce noisy alignments requiring filtering. The domain of the data is limited to publicly available web content.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The SeamlessAlign data is ranked by Sonar alignment scores, allowing users to filter by quality threshold. The paper uses the top 400 hours per X-eng direction and top 200 hours per eng-X direction for training. The full metadata (up to Sonar threshold 1.15) is open-sourced for community use.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Audio preprocessing included: (1) deduplication of audio file URLs, (2) downloading and resampling to 16KHz, (3) filtering non-speech data with a bespoke audio event detection (AED) model, (4) Voice Activity Detection (VAD) segmentation using Silero VAD, (5) over-segmentation to create overlapping splits for mining. Text preprocessing followed NLLB data sources, cleaning, and filtering steps using the Stopes library.
rai:dataSocialImpact: SeamlessAlign enables multilingual speech translation research that can improve accessibility for low-resource language speakers, people with visual impairments, and those without literacy. However, the data was mined from publicly available web sources, and personally identifiable information may not be entirely eliminated. The dataset could also be misappropriated for nefarious activities, and low-resource language communities with lower digital literacy may be more vulnerable to misinformation.
rai:dataUseCases: Training and fine-tuning multilingual speech translation models (S2TT, S2ST); speech-to-text translation research; multimodal machine translation; building speech translation systems for English-Hindi language pair. The metadata is open-sourced to allow the community to rebuild SeamlessAlign and use it for their own purposes, with the optimal threshold tunable based on task.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: SONAR speech and text encoders (multilingual embedding model); ECAPA-TDNN-based speech language identification (LID) model; Silero VAD (Voice Activity Detection); FAISS (GPU-based similarity search library); audio event detection (AED) model for non-speech filtering; XLS-R-based speech encoder for speaker embeddings.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The training data was mined from publicly available sources on the web. Although data cleaning was performed, personally identifiable information may not be entirely eliminated.

null_reasons.rai:annotationsPerItem: SeamlessAlign uses automatic mining, not human annotation per item; no per-item annotation count is applicable.
null_reasons.rai:annotatorDemographics: SeamlessAlign is automatically mined; no human annotators involved in creating the aligned pairs.
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: No inter-annotator agreement or annotation quality analysis; alignment quality is measured via Sonar similarity scores and BLEU evaluation, not human annotation analysis.
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: SeamlessAlign uses automated mining pipeline (Stopes library), not a human annotation platform.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: No specific data collection timeframe is mentioned in the paper for the SeamlessAlign mining process.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: No explicit discussion of missing data handling in the SeamlessAlign pipeline; the paper notes some languages have no mined data (dashes in Table 10) but does not describe a missing data protocol.
null_reasons.rai:dataImputationProtocol: No imputation protocol described; the dataset consists of mined aligned pairs with no imputation of missing values.
null_reasons.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: No versioning or update cadence described for SeamlessAlign; it is released as a static open-source dataset.

evidence.name: we created a multimodal corpus of automatically aligned speech translations, dubbed SeamlessAlign . Filtered and combined with human-labeled and pseudo-labeled data (totaling 406,000 hours), we developed the first multilingual system capable of translating from and into English for both speech and text.
evidence.description: In this section, we describe how we employed parallel data mining to create SeamlessAlign : the largest open dataset for multimodal translation to date, totaling 470,000 hours.
evidence.url: all contributions in this work—including models, inference code, finetuning recipes backed by our improved modeling toolkit Fairseq2 , and metadata to recreate the unfiltered 470,000 hours of SeamlessAlign —are open-sourced and accessible at https://github.com/facebookresearch/seamless_communication .

evidence.isLiveDataset: Since our mined data can help support many different use cases, we are open-sourcing the meta-data for the full amount (i.e., up to a Sonar threshold of 1.15), to allow the community to rebuild SeamlessAlign and use it for their own purposes.
evidence.rai:dataCollection: We start with 4 million hours of raw audio originating from a publicly available repository of crawled web data. Table 10 provides statistics on the amount of raw audio for each language. Approximately 1 million hours in this collection are in English.
evidence.rai:dataCollectionType: We start with 4 million hours of raw audio originating from a publicly available repository of crawled web data.
evidence.rai:dataCollectionRawData: We start with 4 million hours of raw audio originating from a publicly available repository of crawled web data. Table 10 provides statistics on the amount of raw audio for each language.
evidence.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Firstly, we deduplicated the audio file URLs found in the repository, downloaded the audio files, and resampled at 16KHz. Subsequently, we filtered out the non-speech data with a bespoke audio event detection (AED) model.
evidence.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Mining was performed using a margin criterion with our Stopes data processing library. The overall processing is identical to that developed for T2TT mining in NLLB. We performed so-called global mining , where all speech segments in one language are compared to all speech segments in another language.
evidence.rai:machineAnnotationTools: We thus followed the over-segmentation approach drawn from [Duquenne et al., 2021] (as depicted in Figure 1). First, we used an open Voice Activity Detection (VAD) model [Silero, 2021] to split audio files into shorter segments. Subsequently, our speech LID model was used on each file.
evidence.rai:dataUseCases: Since our mined data can help support many different use cases, we are open-sourcing the meta-data for the full amount (i.e., up to a Sonar threshold of 1.15), to allow the community to rebuild SeamlessAlign and use it for their own purposes. The optimal threshold can thus be tuned based on the task, balancing dataset size and alignment quality.
evidence.rai:dataSocialImpact: Regarding data acquisition, the training data used for model development were mined from various publicly available sources on the web. Although we invested heavily in data cleaning, personally identifiable information may not be entirely eliminated.
evidence.rai:dataLimitations: This kind of mining, however, tends to produce noisy alignments and requires some filtering. We use the top 400 hours of SeamlessAlign (see Section 3) in each of 33 X–eng directions and the top 200 hours in each of 29 eng–X directions based on Sonar alignment scores.
evidence.rai:dataBiases: Results show that masculine representation is predominant in most of the datasets. Extremely low representations of gender (i.e., low matching of gendered words based on our selected vocabulary) are found in EuroParl, Fleurs, and Flores datasets.
evidence.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Regarding data acquisition, the training data used for model development were mined from various publicly available sources on the web. Although we invested heavily in data cleaning, personally identifiable information may not be entirely eliminated.
